 JUDGMENT

This suit is filed by the plaintiff against the defendants to declare that the plaintiff is the absolute owner of the suit schedule property bearing site No.411 situated at Nagarabhavi 2 nd Stage, 7th Block, measuring east-west 14.78 meters and north-south 9.14 meters totally measuring 135.08 square meters and also direct the defendant No.1 to quit and deliver the vacant possession of the suit schedule property to the plaintiff.

2. The case of the plaintiff in brief is as hereunder:-
The 2nd defendant Bengaluru Development Authority has acquired certain lands for the purpose of formation of Nagarabhavi layout under preliminary notification dated 15.07.1982 and final notification dated 05.08.1986.

Thereafter, the 2nd defendant had formed layout and when the plaintiff applied for allotment of the site, the suit schedule site No.411 was allotted to her on 07.08.2002 followed by sale deed dated 25.11.2002 registered on 23.01.2003 and possession certificate was also issued on 30.11.2002.
The plaintiff became absolute owner of the suit site.

At the time of registration of the sale deed in her favour, the suit schedule property was within the limits of Rajarajeshwari Nagar CMC, where she had applied the khatha and khata certificate was issued in her name.
Subsequently, the suit schedule site came within the limits of BBMP and therefore the BBMP has also issued a khatha.
In the meanwhile, the plaintiff has mortgaged the suit schedule property and availed loan from Hotel Industrialist Co-operative Bank Limited on 06.05.2014.
The defendant No.1, who is a stranger to the suit schedule property, has illegally constructed a shed in the suit schedule property.

On coming to know the same, the plaintiff made a representation to the Executive Engineer, BDA on 22.12.2012 and to the 2nd defendant on 23.05.2013, requesting them to remove the illegal construction for which the Executive Engineer had issued an endorsement dated 22.07.2013, wherein the plaintiff informed that since the sale deed is already registered, BDA cannot remove the illegal construction and the plaintiff is at liberty to remove the legal constructions in accordance with law.

Thereafter, the plaintiff has lodged a complaint with Jnanabharathi Police station on 02.12.2014 and pursuant to the complaint, when the police summoned defendant No.1, he had revealed that he had instituted a suit in O.S.No.7876/2005 for the relief of permanent injunction against defendant No.2, which came to be dismissed on Ushadevi vs Mani Chetty C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156885263/
2 11.01.2013 and as against it preferred a RFA No.937/2013 before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, which came to be withdrawn as not pressed on 09.07.2014.

He has further revealed that he has filed WP No.50406/2013 questioning the acquisition notifications as they were lapsed and therefore the police have issued an endorsement dated 25.04.2015 to approach the 2nd defendant to resolve the dispute.

As against the same, the plaintiff has approached the Hon'ble High Court by filing a W.P.No.28089/2015 wherein the Hon'ble High Court disposed the writ petition directing the police to take action and reserving liberty to the plaintiff to initiate appropriate criminal and civil proceedings and thereafter, the police have filed charge-sheet against the defendant No.1 for the offences punishable under Section 447 & 506 IPC before the 9 th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru in C.C.No.24021/2016.

sentences.text: Though the plaintiff has obtained a building plan for the construction of the building, due to the civil dispute, she could not construct building in the suit schedule property.

The plaintiff claims cause of action dated 22.07.2013 when 2nd defendant BDA had issued endorsement to the plaintiff directing plaintiff to take suitable action to remove unauthorised shed and subsequently when the Jnanabharathi Police issued an endorsement 25.04.2015 and again on 24.02.2016, when the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in WP No.28089/2015 granted liberty to the plaintiff to initiate appropriate proceedings.
3. Pursuant to the suit summons issued by this Court, the defendant No.1 entered appearance and filed his written statement.

In the written statement filed by the defendant No.1, while denying the title and delivery of possession to the plaintiff, he has contended that the suit schedule property was not taken possession by BDA from its original owners at any point of time.

He has admitted that he has put a shed in the suit schedule property and contended that one Smt.Siddamma and her sons,
being the owners of the suit schedule property, executed a general power of attorney dated 18.02.1987 in favour of one Smt.Jankubai and based on the general power of attorney, the defendant No.1 entered into an agreement and got the physical possession of the property in the year 2000 itself and subsequently got registered sale deed dated 14.03.2005 from Jankubai in his favour.
It is his specific contention that though the sale deed was executed on 14.03.2005, defendant No.1 has been in physical possession of the property right from the year 2000 itself.

It is also contended that its previous owners Siddamma and her sons formed residential layouts and sold the sites to several people and the plaintiff has been in possession of the property prior to the year 2000 by paying full consideration amount to the owners.
It is also pleaded that he has even drilled a Borewell in the suit schedule property and got electricity connection right from the year 2000.

He has further pleaded that the plaintiff as well as BDA was aware about the possession of the erstwhile owners of the suit schedule property and BDA, never took the possession and therefore question of delivery of possession to the plaintiff do not arise.

He has pleaded that his possession is continuous,
uninterrupted and settled.

He has also pleaded that he has been in possession of the suit schedule property for more than 17 years adverse to the right and interest of the plaintiff and therefore he has claimed title and possession even by adverse possession.

He has referred the proceedings of the BDA as the only paper proceedings without taking actual physical possession of the suit schedule property and therefore filed writ petition before the Hon'ble High Court challenging the acquisition proceedings in WP No.50406/2013.

The defendant No.1 has also pleaded that since the BDA was fully aware that the previous owners have formed layout and had already disposed several properties and therefore, even after the allotment of various sites in the same row, subsequently the BDA had allotted alternative sites to the various allottees including to one Sri Revaiah, who was the Ushadevi vs Mani Chetty C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156885263/
3 allottee of site No.412.
4.

Defendant No.1 has further pleaded that the allottees of site No.405, 406, 407, 401, 402, 403,
408, 409 and 410 are allotted alternative sites and therefore it is for the plaintiff to approach the BDA to seek alternative sites.

It is further pleaded that the holder of site Nos.39 and 40 by name Smt.Rajeshwari has filed OS No.4624/2005 seeking the relief of permanent injunction, which came to be decreed against the 2nd defendant on similar grounds.
He has contended that he is also in possession of site No.412 said to have been formed by BDA and he is possessing the larger extent of the site covering the site No.411 and also site No.412.
He has contended that he is entitled to protect possession adverse to the interest of the plaintiff and the 2nd defendant and the suit is also barred by limitation.
On these grounds, he has sought for dismissal of the suit.

5. In the written statement filed by the defendant No.2, it has confirmed the acquisition of the suit schedule property, formation of the suit schedule site, allotment of site to the plaintiff, delivery of the possession and execution of the registered sale deed in favour of the plaintiff and sought for the dismissal of the suit.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, this Court has framed the following issues and addl. Issue No.1:-
1) Whether plaintiff proves that she is the owner of the suit schedule property?
2) Whether plaintiff is entitled for vacant possession of the suit schedule property?
3) Whether plaintiff proves that the first defendant is liable to be permanently restrained from interfering with plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property?
4) Whether Court fee paid is insufficient?
5) Whether suit is barred by law of limitation?
6) Whether plaintiff is entitled for the reliefs sought for?
7) What decree or order?
Additional Issue 1) Whether the defendant No.1 proves that he has perfected title over the suit schedule property by adverse possession as contended by him?
7. In support of the case of the plaintiff, the plaintiff herself examined as PW1 and produced Ex.P1 to 26 documents.
In support of the case of the defendants, defendant No.1 is examined as DW1.
One M. Ravi Kumar, SDA of defendant No.2 is examined as DW2 and one Sri Sanjay, SDA of defendant Ushadevi vs Mani Chetty C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156885263/
4 No.2 is examined as DW3.
Ex.D.20 to 26 are marked on behalf of the second defendant.

Later again,
one Siddaraju P.S. is examined on behalf of defendant No.1 as DW4 in support of the sale agreement and GPA said to be executed in respect of the suit schedule property by the previous owners.
Ex. D.1 to Ex.D.38 are marked on behalf of defendants.
8. Heard the arguments.

9. Findings of this Court on the above issues are as hereunder:
Issue No.1 : In the affirmative Issue No.2 : In the affirmative Issue No.3 : Does not arise for consideration Issue No.4 : In the affirmative Issue No.5 : In the negative Issue No.6 : In the affirmative Addl.
Issue No.1 : In the negative Issue No.7 : As per final order, for the following:

REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- The plaintiff claims title over the suit schedule property on the basis of allotment of the suit schedule site No.411 made in her favour by BDA through the allotment letter dated 16.10.2002 and subsequent sale deed dated 25.11.2002 registered on 23.01.2003 pursuant to the formation of sites by acquiring various lands for the formation of the sites.

On the other hand, the defendant No.1 claims that he has purchased the suit schedule property from one Jankubai who was the power of attorney holder of the original owners through the sale deed dated 14.03.2005.
11.

It is not in dispute that several lands were acquired by the BDA through the preliminary notification dated 15.07.1982 produced at Ex.P19 and the final notification dated 05.08.1986 produced at Ex.P20.

The plaintiff has also relied upon the notification dated 06.10.1987 issued under Section 16(2) of Land Acquisition Act, wherein the BDA said to have taken possession of the land in which the suit schedule site was formed on 09.03.1987.

In addition to this, the plaintiff has also relied upon the land acquisition register extract produced at Ex.P22 for passing of the award and disbursement of the award in the year 1987 in favour of the owners of the land.

12. It is undisputed fact that the defendant No.1 herein challenged the above land acquisition notifications by filing W.P.No.50406/2013 before the Hon'ble High Court, which came to be dismissed on 03.02.2023 as per Ex.P26 and thereby the acquisition of the lands is confirmed.

The plaintiff has produced Ex.P2 allotment letter dated 16.10.2002, Ex.P3 sale deed dated 25.11.2002 registered on 23.01.2003, Ex.P4 possession letter dated 30.11.2002 to establish the transfer of title in favour of the plaintiff.
The defendant No.2 BDA has confirmed it.

Though the defendant No.1 has questioned the acquisition proceedings, the original owners have not questioned it and the defendant No.1 is unsuccessful in seeking the cancellation of the acquisition on the ground that the acquisition was lapsed.

Therefore, when the BDA had acquired it, it has a right to allot the same in favour of the allottees and accordingly it has allotted suit schedule site No.411 to the plaintiff and title is conveyed in respect of the suit schedule property by executing the sale deed dated 25.11.2002.

The defendant No.1 has argued at length contending that the BDA has also recognised that the erstwhile owners have formed layout in the suit schedule property and disposed several sites and Ushadevi vs Mani Chetty C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156885263/
5 hence the BDA has allotted alternative sites in the same row to various allottees and therefore, the acquisition proceedings cannot be recognised by the court to hold the passing of title to the plaintiff.
But, even if alternative sites were allotted to other allottees of the sites, when the acquisition of the suit schedule property by BDA is confirmed by the Hon'ble High Court, it is not open to this court to hold that the acquisition was not in accordance with law.
Therefore, these arguments submitted on behalf of the defendant No.1 cannot be accepted.
13. The defendant No.1 has also taken up a contention of perfection of title by adverse possession and the suit is barred by limitation.
The court has framed issue No.5 and additional issue in this regard.
The same will be answered while answering issue No.5 and additional issue No.1.

Hence,
keeping open the finding on issue No.5 and additional issue No.1, the court holds that a valid title conveyed in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the suit schedule site through the sale deed dated 25.11.2002.

Though the defendant No.1 has relied upon Ex.D2 sale deed dated 14.03.2005 to establish his title over the suit schedule property, when the court has recorded a finding that the suit schedule property was acquired through the preliminary notification dated 15.07.1982 as per Ex.P19 and final notification dated 05.08.1986 as per Ex.P20, the land vests with the Government immediately after passing of final notification and therefore, the original owners have lost their title after the final notification issued by the Government.
In view of this, the original owner had no marketable title to convey title in respect of the suit schedule property in favour of defendant No.1.

In view of this, either the general power of attorney dated 18.02.1987 produced at Ex.D53 or the sale agreement dated 25.02.2000 executed by the power of attorney holder of original owners in favour of the defendant No.1 or the Ex.D33(a) affidavit cannot convey any right, title or interest over the suit schedule property either in favour of one Smt.Jankubai, who is stated to be the power of attorney holder of original owners or in favour of the defendant No.1 in anyway.
Added to this, the sale deed executed in favour of the plaintiff is anterior in point of time from the sale deed of the defendant No.1.
Therefore, the defendant No.1 has not derived any title over the suit schedule property on the basis of the sale deed produced at Ex.D.2 dated 14.03.2005.
Accordingly, the court holds that the plaintiff has proved his title over the suit schedule property.
Consequently, issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.5 and Additional Issue No.1:-

In the written statement filed by the defendant No.1, he has taken up a contention that even if preliminary and final notifications were issued in respect of the suit schedule property, the BDA has not taken possession of the suit schedule property at any point of time and the original owners Smt.Siddamma and her children formed layout in the larger extent of their property sold various sites to several purchasers and on 18.02.1987, they have executed a general power of attorney in favour of one Smt.Jankubai and based on the said general power of attorney, the defendant No.1 has entered into an agreement of sale and got the physical possession of the property in the year 2000 and subsequently the sale deed was registered in his favour on 14.03.2005.
The defendant No.1 has asserted his physical possession over the suit schedule property from the year 2000 itself on the basis of GPA.

He has also pleaded that the possession claimed by the BDA is only a paper possession without taking actual physical possession and on the other hand, the possession of the defendant No.1 is continuous, uninterrupted, settled and adverse to the right and interest of the plaintiff as well as BDA, which continued for more than 17 years and thereby he has perfected his title by adverse possession against the plaintiff and second Ushadevi vs Mani Chetty C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156885263/
6 defendant.
15.

It is well settled law from catena of decisions including from the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court rendered in the case of Ravinder Kaur Grewal and others v/s Manjit Kaur and others (2019)8 SCC 729 relied upon by the learned counsel appearing for defendant No.1 that the possession,
however, for any length of time will not automatically partake the character of adverse possession,
unless the necessary ingredients are established.

entities.text: Ravinder Kaur Grewal and others v/s Manjit Kaur and others (2019)8 SCC 729
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also well settled law that the party who claims adverse possession is required to prove that when he came into possession of the property, when the possession becomes adverse by establishing that the possession is adequate in continuity, adequate in publicity adverse to the owner in denial of the title of the owner to his knowledge, visible,
notorious and peaceful.

In this regard, in the decision relied upon by the learned counsel appearing for defendant No.1 in para No.23 the Hon'ble Supreme Court by relying upon its previous decisions rendered in the case of Karnataka Board of Work v/s Union of India (2004)10 SCC 779 held that a person who is trying to defeat the rights of true owner has no equities in his favour and heavy burden lies on him to clearly plead and establish all facts necessary to establish his adverse possession in the following words:-
"30.

entities.text: Karnataka Board of Work v/s Union of India (2004)10 SCC 779
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Karnataka Board of Wakf, the law was stated, thus:(SCCp.785,para11) '11.
In the eye of the law, an owner would be deemed to be in possession of a property so long as there is no intrusion.
Non-use of the property by the owner even for a long time won't affect his title.
But the position will be altered when another person takes possession of the property and asserts a right over it.
Adverse possession is a hostile possession by clearly asserting hostile title in denial of the title of the true owner.

It is a well-settled principle that a party claiming adverse possession must prove that his possession is 'nec vi, nec clam, nec precario', that is, peaceful, open and continuous.
The possession must be adequate in continuity, in publicity, and in extent to show that their possession is adverse to the true owner.
It must start with a wrongful disposition of the rightful owner and be actual, visible, exclusive, hostile and continued over the statutory period.
(See S.M. Karim v. Bibi Sakina, Parsinni v. Sukhi and D.N. Venkatarayappa v. State of Karnataka).

entities.text: D.N. Venkatarayappa v. State of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Physical fact of exclusive possession and the animus possidendi to hold as owner in exclusion to the actual owner are the most important factors that are to be accounted in case of this nature.
Plea of adverse possession is not a pure question of law but a blended one of fact and law.

Therefore,
a person who claims adverse possession should show: (a) on what date he came into possession, (b) what was the nature of his possession, (c) whether the factum of possession was known to the other party,
(d) how long his possession has continued, and (e) his possession was open and undisturbed.
A person pleading adverse possession has no equities in his favour.

Since he is trying to defeat the rights of the true owner, it is for him to clearly plead and establish all facts necessary to establish his adverse possession' ".

7 16.

sentences.text: Again, in para No.60 of the aforesaid judgement, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has stressed the requirements to be pleaded and proved in the following words.

"60. The adverse possession requires all the three classic requirements to co-exist at the same time, namely, nec vi i.e., adequate in continuity, nec lam i.e., adequate in publicity and nec precario i.e., adverse to a competitor, in denial of title and his knowledge.
Visible, notorious and peaceful so that if the owner does not take care to know notorious facts, knowledge is attributed to him on the basis that but for due diligence he would have known it.
Adverse possession cannot be decreed on a title which is not pleaded.
Animus possidendi under hostile colour of title is required.
Trespasser's long possession is not synonymous without adverse possession.
Trespasser's possession is construed to be on behalf of the owner, the casual user does not constitute adverse possession.
The owner can take possession from a trespasser at any point in time.

Possessor looks after the property, protects it and in case of agricultural property by and large the concept is that actual tiller should own the land who works by dint of his hard labour and makes the land cultivable.
The legislature in various States confers rights based on possession".
17. In view of the above, a person who claims adverse possession is required to clearly plead as to how the possession become adverse.

In the present case in para No.13 of the written statement filed by defendant No.1, he has pleaded that he came into possession of the suit schedule property in the year 2000 itself when one Jankubai the power of attorney holder of original owners has executed a sale agreement in his favour on the basis of the power of attorney dated 18.02.1987.

It is important to note that though the defendant No.1 has produced the general power of attorney dated 18.02.1987 executed by the original owner in favour of Jankubai, the power of attorney do not indicate that the possession was delivered to Jankubai by the original owners.

The other document relied upon by the learned counsel appearing for the defendant No.1 is an affidavit said to be executed on 18.02.1987 as per Ex.D33(a) and on the basis of this affidavit, the learned counsel appearing for defendant No.1 has contended that the possession was delivered to Jankubai.
But, the defendant No.1 has not pleaded about this Ex.D33(a) affidavit in his written statement.
Needless to mention that a possession of immovable property cannot be transferred by way of affidavit.
Even otherwise, there is nothing on record to show that Smt.Jankubai was in possession of the suit schedule site on the basis of this affidavit.
If she was in possession of the property, certainly she would have produced some documents either for cultivating it or for enjoying it by paying tax or putting up some building in it.
It is not the case of the defendant No.1 that she had constructed any building in it or enjoyed it in any way.
Therefore Ex.D33(a) cannot be considered as evidence for delivery of possession in favour of Jankubai.
18. It is also necessary to note that the defendant No.1 has claimed title over the suit schedule property through Ex.D2 sale deed dated 14.03.2005.
In Ex.D2, there is no reference either about the sale agreement or affidavit relied upon by the defendant No.1 produced at Ex.D33(a) and Ex.D34.
On the other hand, the recital of Ex.D2 sale deed indicates that the possession of the suit schedule property was delivered by Jankubai in favour of defendant No.1 for the first time on 14.03.2005.
Ex.D2 is a bilateral contract between him and Jankubai.

Defendant No.1 has accepted the sale deed Ushadevi vs Mani Chetty C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156885263/
8 by admitting the contents therein regarding the delivery of possession on 14.03.2005.

Therefore,
when the defendant No.1 claims delivery of possession on the basis of sale deed dated 14.03.2005,
his contention to the effect that the possession was delivered in the year 2000 itself is self contradictory and cannot be accepted.

19. It is an admitted fact that the plaintiff has instituted O.S.No.7876/2005 against the second defendant BDA for the relief of permanent prohibitory injunction to restrain the BDA from interfering with his possession over the suit schedule property.
The certified copy of its judgement is produced by the plaintiff at Ex.P15.
Ex . P15

shows that immediately after getting the sale deed as per Ex.D2, the defendant No.1 has filed this suit against the BDA, wherein he has pleaded that he has acquired the possession over the suit schedule property through the sale deed dated 14.03.2005.
While filing OS No.7876/2005, defendant No.1 has not pleaded that he has taken the possession in the year 2000 itself.

It is also important to note that though he has taken a contention that after the purchase of the property, his vendors have constructed a small house and it is let out by him to the tenant, this contention is inconsistent with his written statement that he has constructed a shed in it.
As rightly pointed out by the learned counsel appearing for the plaintiff, the description given by the plaintiff in O.S.No.7876/2005 do not reflect the existence of any shed in it.
The schedule given in O.S.No.7876/2005 indicates that it was a vacant site.
The plaintiff was unsuccessful in O.S.No.7876/2005 and the suit filed by him came to be dismissed, holding that he has failed to prove his possession.

The said suit came to be dismissed on 11.01.2013 as per Ex.P15 holding that when he has failed to produce the layout plan to establish that the original owners have formed the site, mere mentioning of the site number in the sale deed does not create right or possession over the property.
Therefore, the plaintiff has failed to prove possession in O.S.No.7876/2005 filed in the year 2005 which came to be dismissed in the year 2013.
As against this judgement, the defendant No.1 has preferred RFA No.937/2013 as per Ex.P12 and it was withdrawn.
Thereby the possessory right claimed by the plaintiff over the suit schedule property is abandoned by him.

When the court has already recorded a finding in O.S.No.7876/2005 that the plaintiff has failed to prove his possession from the year 2005 to 2013, which is confirmed by withdrawal of appeal filed by the defendant No.1, the defendant No.1 is estopped from re-agitating the possessory right atleast from the date of the suit until its disposal i.e., from the year 2005 to 2013.

The reason is that when the court has already recorded a finding that he is not in possession of the suit schedule property, at this stage, the court cannot record a finding that the plaintiff was in possession of the suit schedule property during the period of litigation held in O.S.No.7876/2005.
20.

Learned counsel appearing for defendant No.1 relied upon a representation given by plaintiff on 21.12.2012 to the Executive Engineer, BDA as per Ex.D1 and vehemently contended that in that representation, the plaintiff has pleaded that a lady staying nearby had obstructed the plaintiff from taking possession of the sites.

Relying upon this statement, learned counsel appearing for the defendant No.1 has strongly contended that this document clearly shows that the possession was never delivered to the plaintiff and she has not taken the possession at any point of time.

As rightly contended by the learned counsel appearing for the defendant No.1, the statement given in Ex.D1 by the plaintiff indicates that a lady had obstructed her from taking possession and therefore she has given representation in the year 2012.
Therefore, the court is required to examine whether the defendant No.1 has established adverse possession in the light of Ex.D1 statement.

It is pertinent to Ushadevi vs Mani Chetty C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156885263/
9 note that in Ex.D1, the plaintiff has not stated that the obstruction was caused by the defendant No.1.
On the other hand, the reference in Ex.D1 shows that the obstruction was caused by a lady.

Therefore, though Ex.D1 can be considered to hold that the plaintiff did not get the possession of the suit schedule property, it is not helpful to the defendant No.1 to show that he is the person obstructed the plaintiff from taking possession.
In order to prove the adverse possession, the defendant No.1 must establish that his possession was hostile to the plaintiff.
Ex.D1 do not help the defendant No.1 for this assertion of his defence.
21. As already observed above, in order to establish the adverse possession, the possession must be in continuity, adequate in publicity, notorious and peaceful.

In other words, a person who claims adverse possession must establish that he was in peaceful possession of the property for a period of more than 12 years from the date when his possession become adverse.
In the present case, there is no evidence to show that right from the purchase of the suit schedule property by the defendant No.1 through Ex.D2, he was in peaceful possession of the property.

As already observed above, the claim made by the defendant No.1 in Ex.P15 judgement produced in respect of O.S.No.7876/2005 filed by him against BDA shows that though the BDA has no manner of right over the property, the officials of BDA came near the property on 04.10.2005 and tried to dispossess the defendant No.1's tenant and threatened to demolish the building stating that BDA has acquired the property.
Therefore, the vendor of the plaintiff has questioned the possession of the defendant No.1 on 04.10.2005 itself.
Hence, the defendant No.1 had to file O.S.No.7876/2005 and after the dismissal of the suit, he has filed WP No.50406/2013 challenging the acquisition notification.
It came to be dismissed on 03.02.2023 after filing of the suit.
In the meantime, the plaintiff has instituted this suit in the year 2017.
Therefore, the documents produced by the defendant No.1 itself shows that his possession was not peaceful.
It was initially questioned by BDA and later by the plaintiff.
In order to attract adverse possession, the defendant No.1 has to show that his possession was not questioned at least for a period of 12 years.
On the other hand, in the present case, the possession of the defendant No.1 was questioned from the very year of sale deed obtained by him and throughout.

Therefore,
one of the important ingredient which is required to be proved to establish the adverse possession is not proved by the plaintiff.
22. In order to establish the adverse possession, the defendant No.1 is also required to prove that on which date his possession become adverse.
Either in the written statement or in the evidence, the defendant No.1 has neither pleaded nor deposed before the court.
The defendant No.1 has not even pleaded and proved as to when his possession was made known to the plaintiff.
It is also necessary to note that though the defendant No.1 has taken up a contention that a shed is constructed in it,
admittedly
, no license is obtained.
He has also taken up a contention that he has drilled a borewell and electricity connection is obtained.
But there is nothing on record to substantiate the same.

Therefore, though there is evidence to show that a shed is constructed in the suit schedule site, in the written statement, while pleading that he has put up a construction of house, the date of construction is not pleaded.

Therefore, the required ingredients to establish the adverse possession is not made out by defendant No.1.
23.

Learned counsel appearing for defendant No.1 has stressed on the point that though the BDA said to have taken possession on the property by Ex.P21 notification on 09.03.1987, the mahazar for Ushadevi vs Mani Chetty C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156885263/
10 having taken possession of the suit schedule site is not produced before the court and therefore adverse inference has to be drawn.

In this regard, he has relied upon evidence given on behalf of defendant No.2 by DW2 and 3 and contended that inspite of specific direction given by Hon'ble High Court in WP No.21055/2024 dated 07.08.2024 BDA has failed to produce the mahazar and in the absence of taking of physical possession, the plaintiff cannot claim possession over the suit schedule property through the sale deed executed by BDA.
As rightly contended by the learned counsel appearing for defendant No.1, inspite of the direction given to BDA, it has not produced the mahazar in proof of taking possession of the property.

But, learned counsel appearing for the plaintiff has relied upon the Full Bench decision of our Hon'ble High Court in the case of ITI Employees Housing Co-operative Society Limited, Bangalore v/s Venkatappa 2010(4) Kar.L.J.19 (FB) wherein the Hon'ble High Court, while holding that it is necessary to take actual physical possession held that it is one of the mode of taking possession and when it is notified by the Deputy Commissioner in the official gazette, the land vests with the government and therefore even in the absence of production of mahazar since the notification of taking possession is published in the official gazette, it is a sufficient proof of taking possession.

sentences.text: Ex.P21 notification shows that the possession was taken on 09.03.1987.
It is published in the official gazette.
It was made known to the general public.
When a publication was issued in the gazette in respect of a vacant property, the general public cannot claim that possession was not taken.
It is equally applicable to the defendant No.1 also.

It is not in dispute that as on the date of Ex.P21 notification in the year 1987 it was vacant,
such being the case publication of the gazette notification in respect of a vacant property is sufficient to hold that the possession was taken though the mahazar is not produced.
If the property consists of a building, the circumstances would have been different.
In case of vacant land, normally the possession follows the title.

When the acquisition of the suit schedule property is confirmed by the Hon'ble High Court, the possession follows the title and the production of Ex.P21 notification is sufficient to hold that the BDA has taken possession.

Apart from that, when the defendant No.1 has challenged the land acquisition by filing WP No.50406/2013 in the order dated 03.02.2023 passed by the Hon'ble High Court as per Ex.P26, the Hon'ble High Court has categorically observed that the possession of the suit schedule property was also taken on 09.03.1987 and observed that the status of defendant No.1 is not much different from the trespassers.

In this regard, the Hon'ble High Court in WP No.50406/2013 filed by defendant No.1 in the order dated 03.02.2023 observed as hereunder:-
"3. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition Papers, this Court declines indulgence in the matter, for the following reasons:
(a) The Preliminary Notification is of July 1982 and Final Notification is of August 1986, the award was passed on 8.2.1987 and the same was approved on 27.2.1987.
The possession of the land was taken by drawing the mahazar on 9.3.1987.
The Notification u/s 16(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was gazetted on 29.10.1987.
Thus, the lands have vested in the State, as rightly submitted by learned counsel for the BDA.
These petitions have been filed only on 8.11.2013.
Thus, there is enormous delay & latches that remain unexplained.
The courts do not come to the aid of sleepy & tardy, say the sages of law.

sentences.text: (b) The submission of learned counsel for the Petitioners that Petitioners were before the Civil Court in O.S.Nos.7875/2005 & 7877/2005, disposed off on 18.08.2009 and later, the same is challenged before this Court in R.F.A.No.149/2010 that came to be disposed off on 15.07.2013 and therefore, all this would constitute a plausible explanation to the delay brooked, is bit difficult to countenance.
No explanation is offered by the C/W WP Nos. 50405/2013,50406/2013 Petitioners for the delay brooked between the Final Notification of August 1986 and the filing of the suits in question in 2005.
There is already Preliminary Notification, followed by the Final Notification, that eventually resulted into passing of the award and possession is also taken.

That being the position, no relief can be granted to the Petitioners who have been clinging on to the property only on the basis of some interim order granted in the suit and later, in the Regular First Appeal, which have been dismissed subsequently.
(c) After the acquisition is accomplished, the land would vest in the State and the so called land owners continuing in the occupation, are not much different from the trespassers.
The law does not come to the protection of such persons.
An argument to the contrary would offend the sense of reason, law & justice.

In the above circumstances, these petitions being devoid of merits, are liable to be dismissed &
accordingly, they are, costs having been made easy.

This judgment does not come in the way of Petitioners claiming the compensation or other benefit,
in accordance with law, by establishing their credentials.
In that connection, all contentions are kept open".

24. In addition to this, ExP13 is the order passed in the writ petition filed by the plaintiff in W.P.No.28089/2015 dated 24.02.216 against Government, BDA, Police and the defendant No.1 herein challenging the endorsement given by the police, refusing to register criminal case.
In the said order while the Hon'ble High Court has also reiterated the unauthorised occupation of the defendant No.1 in the suit schedule property in the following words:-

"3. It would appear that the petitioner would have both civil and criminal remedies insofar as the ejectment of the seventh respondent who is in unauthorized occupation of the land, notwithstanding that Respondent No.7 may be claiming by way of a sale deed executed by the original owner of the land.
Since admittedly, the land has been acquired by the BDA and thereafter has been transferred in favour of the petitioner as a house site, the petitioner cannot be denied her due.
She is entitled to initiate both criminal and civil proceedings against the seventh respondent.

The police would not be right to have stated that in view of the pendency of the writ petition in W.P.50406/2013, the petitioner shall not initiate criminal proceedings against the seventh respondent.
There is no such impediment.

The police are directed to take such action, in accordance with law".
25.

In view of the reasons stated above, the evidence adduced by the defendant No.1 is highly insufficient hold that he has perfected the title over the suit schedule property by adverse Ushadevi vs Mani Chetty C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156885263/
12 possession.
Further, he has failed to prove that the suit filed by the plaintiff for declaration of title is barred by limitation.
Hence issue No.5 and additional issue No.1 is answered in the negative.
26. Issue No.4:- The defendant No.1 has taken up a contention that the court fee paid is insufficient.
The plaintiff has valued the suit property at Rs.62,52,200/- and paid court fee of Rs.2,25,908/-.
There is nothing on record to show that the valuation made by the plaintiff in respect of the suit schedule property was incorrect.
Therefore, the plaintiff valued the suit schedule property properly and paid proper court fee.
Consequently, issue No.4 is answered in the affirmative.
27. Issues No.2, 6 & 7:-

While answering issue No.1 and addl. issue No.1, this court has held that the plaintiff has proved the title of the suit schedule property and the defendant No.1 has failed to establish the extinguishment of the title of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property by adverse possession.
One of the contention raised on behalf of the defendant No.1 is that there is no cause of action to institute the suit.

In the plaint, the plaintiff has pleaded that the cause of action arose on 22.07.2013 when the defendant No.2 BDA has issued an endorsement to the plaintiff to take suitable action and when the police have issued endorsement on 25.04.2015 and again on 24.02.2016 when the Hon'ble High Court in WP No.28089/2015 granted liberty to initiate the suitable civil and criminal proceedings.
It is contended by the defendant No.1 that the above facts do not give cause of action to the plaintiff..
But, while answering the issue No.1, this court has held that the plaintiff is the absolute owner of the suit schedule property.
The owner of a property has a right to recover the possession of the property unless the defendant is able to prove adverse possession.
While answering addl. issue No.1, this court has held that the defendant No.1 has failed to prove the adverse possession.
The period of 12 years limitation prescribed begins to run from the day when the possession become adverse.
Therefore, when the defendant No.1 has failed to prove the adverse possession, there is no period of limitation to sue for possession.

Under these circumstances, when the plaintiff has pleaded that the defendant No.1 has been illegally squatting over the suit schedule property and inspite of lodging the complaint before the police, she could not take back the possession, she is entitled to sue for possession.
Therefore, this contention of the defendant No.1 cannot be accepted.
28. Learned counsel appearing for defendant No.1 has also disputed the identity of the property to decree the suit in favour of the plaintiff.
The defendant No.1 has not pleaded and disputed the identity of the suit schedule property.
The existence of the site is not in dispute.
The layout plan clearly indicates the identity of the site.

On the other hand, in the written statement filed by defendant No.1 in para No.15, he has pleaded that he has been in physical possession of even in site No.412 and he is in possession of larger extent of site covering site No.411 and also site No.412.
It clearly shows that he is in possession of the site No.411, which is the suit schedule property.
Therefore, he has not even pleaded that any other portion of site No.411 is in the possession of any other person.
Therefore, there is no confusion with the identity of the property.

29. In para No.21 of the written statement, the defendant No.1 has pleaded that holder of site No.39 and 40 by Smt.Rajeshwari filed O.S.No.4624/2005 and obtained a decree of permanent injunction,
which is produced by him at Ex.D19.
It is in respect of a different property and there is nothing on record to show that she is in possession of the suit schedule site or any portion thereof.

Though she Ushadevi vs Mani Chetty C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156885263/
13 has obtained a decree in her favour against BDA, it is only against wrongful dispossession as clarified by the Hon'ble High Court in RSA No.473/2015 filed by BDA against Smt.Rajeshwari,
wherein the Hon'ble High Court, while disposing the appeal observed that BDA is entitled to take possession of the property by initiating appropriate legal proceedings in accordance with law.
The present suit is filed not for an order of prohibitory injunction, but for declaration of title and possession.
Therefore, the suit filed by said Smt.Rajeshwari has no relevance to the present set of facts and the relief claimed by the plaintiff.
In view of these reasons, none of the defence raised by the defendant No.1 is capable of non-suiting the plaintiff from seeking the relief of declaration, title and possession.
Consequently issue No.2, 6 & 7 are answered in the affirmative.
30. Issue No.3:-
The plaintiff has also sought the relief of permanent prohibitory injunction against defendant No.1.
The main suit is filed for declaration of title and recovery of possession.

When the suit is decreed and defendant No.1 is directed to deliver the possession to the plaintiff, the court cannot infer that even after delivery of possession, the defendant No.1 would interfere with the possession of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property.
Therefore, in the present suit, the court need not pass any orders for prohibitory injunction against defendant No.1.

On these observations,
issue No.3 does not arise for consideration and the following order is passed:-
ORDER Suit is decreed with cost.
It is declared that the plaintiff is the absolute owner of the suit property.
The defendant No.1 is directed to quit and deliver the vacant possession of the suit schedule property to the plaintiff within 90 days from today.
Draw decree accordingly.
